problem: Prior embodied active-learning work treats each scene independently and explores only locally around the spawn point. It ignores how an agent's accumulated perception knowledge from earlier buildings should change its exploration and annotation-request behavior in new ones.
motivation: Perception models degrade in new environments, and annotating every viewpoint is impractical. An agent that already has a coarse perception model should skip annotating familiar content and spend its annotation budget on novel parts of a scene. This calls for agents that adapt to the current quality of their perception over a lifetime of buildings.
key_idea: Frame embodied lifelong perception learning as agents that explore buildings with a global frontier mapper plus local point-goal navigation and request annotations to refine a segmentation network that persists across scenes, using a PPO-trained RL agent that jointly learns navigation and annotation with a perception reward.
insight: Only the learned RL agent and the accuracy oracle change their behavior in the lifelong setting (more area per annotation, larger mIoU gains). Uniform and random annotation cannot adapt, so their lifelong gains are small. Appendix ablations show the accuracy-reward term, navigation pre-training and global-frontier exploration are needed for this adaptive behavior. Also, about 20 scene-specific annotations match a model pre-trained on 10,000 views from other buildings (mIoU 0.330).
method: Global navigation: a mapper builds a 2D top-down navigable/obstacle map from depth and pose. Closest-frontier exploration selects a frontier, and the Dijkstra shortest path is split at direction changes into local point-goal targets.

Segmentation network: ImageNet-pretrained dilated ResNet-50 with output stride 8 and 40 classes. It is fine-tuned online after each Annotate action, until minibatch accuracy reaches 95% or 1000 iterations. Weights persist across episodes in the lifelong setup.

RL agent policy: actions are MoveForward, RotateLeft, RotateRight and Annotate. The state is RGB, current segmentation, the last annotation propagated to the current view via optical flow, depth, and the polar local goal (r, φ). A CNN and an MLP branch feed an LSTM (256 hidden units) and a softmax over 4 actions.
Perception reward: change in mIoU on 32 reference views (top-10 classes) after refinement, minus an annotation penalty 0.01, plus a bonus 0.01 for annotating when current-view accuracy is below 0.7.
Exploration reward: decrease in geodesic distance to the local goal plus a bonus of 1 on reaching it. It is combined with the perception reward as λ·R_exp + (1-λ)·R_seg, λ=0.01.

Training: PPO (RLlib) with 10^6 steps of point-goal navigation pre-training using GT segmentation and no Annotate, then 10^6 steps in the full environment (~4 days on 2 Titan X). The segmentation net is reset every 10th episode, with a lightweight 9-layer segmentation net used during RL training.

Heuristic baselines: an accuracy oracle annotates when view accuracy is below 0.7 using GT, uniform annotates every 20th step, and random annotates with probability 5%. All use the same frontier exploration.

setting.backbone: RL policy (CNN+MLP+LSTM, PPO, trained from scratch) plus ResNet-50 segmentation net (ImageNet-pretrained, refined online)
setting.training_data: Policy trained on the 61 Matterport3D train scenes for 1M nav pre-training steps plus 1M steps in the full environment. Segmentation labels come only from agent-requested annotations. The optional pretrained baseline uses 10,000 random train views.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + pose (mapper and optical-flow propagation), plus current segmentation and propagated last annotation
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MoveForward, RotateLeft, RotateRight, Annotate (with a global frontier planner supplying local point goals)
setting.privileged: GT segmentation annotations on request (the query oracle) and GT mask reference views during RL reward computation. The accuracy-oracle baseline uses GT segmentation. Depth and pose are assumed available.

numbers.eval_set_note: 18 test scenes, one episode per scene, max 2000 steps
numbers.extra: segmentation net kept across scenes; mIoU averaged after annotations 1-50 and 51-100

numbers.backbone: heuristic annotation using GT accuracy + ResNet-50
numbers.extra: uses GT segmentation to decide annotation (upper bound baseline)

numbers_note: Custom task with no standard benchmark. Table 1 also has uniform and random baselines. The ablation table (11 val scenes) is not included as own-method rows.
results: In the lifelong setup the RL-agent annotates less frequently (dA/annot 1.070 vs 0.876 episodic) and gains +0.038 mIoU on annotations 1-50, more than uniform (+0.014) or random (+0.007). It is second only to the GT-using accuracy oracle. About 20 scene-specific annotations match a model pretrained on 10,000 views from other buildings (mIoU 0.330).
limitations: Relies on GT depth and pose, with GT annotations available on request, in the simulator only, and evaluated on just 18 test scenes with a single episode each.

Costly RL training (~4 days) using a simplified segmentation net in training but ResNet-50 at test. The RL agent still trails the accuracy oracle, and the absolute gains from lifelong learning are modest.
builds_on: Embodied Visual Active Learning for Semantic Segmentation (Nilsson et al. 2020)
